metrics.label: Population
metrics.description: Resident population.
metrics.method: WorldPop 2020 pixels summed per hex, rescaled so every district (LKA) / county (USA) matches the official 2023 estimate.

metrics.label: Land area
metrics.description: Land area inside the country boundary.
metrics.method: Sum of raster-pixel areas whose centres fall inside the admin boundaries.

metrics.label: UNESCO World Heritage Sites
metrics.description: UNESCO World Heritage Sites (cultural, natural and mixed) located in the country.
metrics.method: Wikidata items with P1435 = Q9259 (non-deprecated, no end date) and P17 = country, grouped by the numeric part of the World Heritage Site id (P757; '72bis'/'72ter' -> 72); component items without an id are merged into a site within 3 km. The representative item is the member with the most Wikipedia sitelinks that has a coordinate inside the country grid (coordinates are tried in turn: grid cell, snap within 6 H3 rings, else nearest land hex within 250 km). Sites whose coordinates are all outside the 50 states + DC (US territories, Mexico-only El Camino Real de Tierra Adentro, foreign components of transnational sites) are dropped. kind from the selection criteria (P2614): (i)-(vi) cultural, (vii)-(x) natural, both mixed. inscribed = earliest P580 start time of the designation (year).

metrics.label: National park visitors
metrics.description: Annual visitors to national parks (USA: recreation visits; Sri Lanka: ticketed local + foreign visitors).
metrics.method: USA: NPS IRMA Stats Annual Park Ranking Report, calendar year 2025, Recreation Visits, Park Type = National Park (64 units); National Park of American Samoa and Virgin Islands NP (territories) are dropped, leaving 62 parks in the 50 states. Coordinates and area (P2046) from the Wikidata item of each park (instance of Q34918903, matched on normalised names: 'NP' -> National Park, 'NP & PRES' -> National Park and Preserve). Sri Lanka: SLTDA Year in Review 2025 Table 19 (Department of Wildlife Conservation), local + foreign visitors per park in 2025. Of its 23 rows, 'Eth Athuru Sevana' (the Udawalawe Elephant Transit Home, a rehabilitation facility) and 'Mirissa' (whale-watching tickets, not an area) are excluded, leaving 21 national parks, marine parks and sanctuaries (2,212,802 of the 2,604,243 visitors). 'Samanala Adaviya' is read as the Peak Wilderness Sanctuary and 'Bareef - Kalpitiya' as the Bar Reef Marine Sanctuary; Kalawewa and Girithale are located at the Kala Wewa and Giritale reservoirs (Wikidata). Coordinates from Wikidata; area_km2 from the WDPA polygon (GIS area) where the park is in WDPA, else Wikidata. Definitions differ: NPS counts recreation visits (person-entries, estimated from traffic counts for most parks); DWC counts tickets sold.

metrics.label: Museums
metrics.description: Museums with coordinates documented in Wikidata (count of points).
metrics.method: Wikidata items instance of museum (Q33506) or any subclass (art, history, science, house museums...), country P17 = Sri Lanka / United States, with coordinates; items with a dissolution (P576) or closure (P3999) date are dropped, one row per item (first coordinate). Points that do not snap to the country grid (US territories) are dropped. Coverage reflects Wikidata completeness, not an official museum census (the US IMLS universe lists far more institutions).

metrics.label: Protected area
metrics.description: Share of the hex area covered by designated protected areas (any IUCN category).
metrics.method: Union of WDPCA polygons with status Designated / Inscribed / Established, excluding UNESCO-MAB Biosphere Reserves (Protected Planet convention) and Proposed sites; all IUCN categories incl. 'Not Reported'. Coverage = share of the hex's H3 child-cell centres (res+3 = 343 points per hex for Sri Lanka, res+2 = 49 for the USA) that fall inside any polygon (shapely STRtree). Computed for every grid hex (land and coastal water, 0 where none); marine protected areas count in water hexes. Sri Lanka's polygons are full resolution; US polygons were generalised server-side (maxAllowableOffset 0.005 deg ~ 500 m). WDPA point-only records (no boundary) are not counted.

metrics.label: Strictly protected area (IUCN Ia-IV)
metrics.description: Share of the hex area covered by protected areas in IUCN categories Ia, Ib, II, III or IV.
metrics.method: As protected_pct, restricted to polygons whose iucn_cat is Ia, Ib, II, III or IV (strict reserves, wilderness, national parks, natural monuments, habitat/species management areas).

metrics.label: Protected area
metrics.description: Area of the hex (land or sea) inside designated protected areas.
metrics.method: protected_pct / 100 x H3 cell area. Overlapping designations are counted once.

metrics.label: GDP (Gold)
metrics.description: Gross domestic product at current prices, US dollars.
metrics.method: USA: BEA CAGDP2, year 2024, current dollars (thousands x 1,000). Lines: total = 1; agriculture = 3 (NAICS 11); industry = 6 + 10 + 11 + 13 + 25 (mining, utilities, construction, durable + nondurable manufacturing); services = total - agriculture - industry (includes government, line 83); manufacturing = 13 + 25 (= line 12); finance = 51 + 56 + 60 (finance & insurance; real estate & rental/leasing; professional, scientific & technical services). Suppressed '(D)' county cells (18,737 in 2024; BEA suppresses complementary cells, so no identity has a single unknown) are estimated for the 20 leaf industries that partition line 2 (private industries) by multi-margin iterative proportional fitting within each state, seeded with ACS 2024 5-year C24030 employment of the matching industry (+1). Margins: every disclosed county aggregate (lines 2, 91, 92, 87, 12, 50, 59, 68, 75, 88, 89, 90, minus its disclosed leaves) and every state leaf total (state value minus disclosed counties). County private totals are reproduced exactly and state industry totals to within 0.01 %; national sector totals equal the sum of BEA state rows. BEA combination areas (23 Virginia county + independent-city combinations, Maui + Kalawao) are split to Census 2023 counties pro rata to 2023 population. Totals are the sum of the 50 states + DC (BEA's US total also includes overseas federal activity, ~0.5 %). Allocation to hexes: population-weighted within each county. gdp_usd = line 1 (all-industry total). | Sri Lanka: Province level (2024, current market prices, Rs mn): national GVA by sector from DCS Statistical Abstract 2025 Table 10.2 (agriculture = A&F&F; industry = manufacturing, mining & other industries + construction; services = the seven service activities). Provincial shares of each sector: the shares quoted from the CBSL PGDP 2024 release are used directly (agriculture: NW 20.0, C 13.9, S 11.8; industry: W 47.6, NW 12.0, C 9.6; services: W 44.5, C 10.7, NW 10.1 %); Western agriculture is the residual that makes Western's GVA share equal its published GDP share (42.4 %); the remaining share of each sector is split among the other provinces in proportion to their 2020 CBSL provincial GVA in that sector (DOSE v2.9, 2010-base series). Net taxes on products (taxes 2,641,646 - subsidies 39,873) are allocated pro rata to provincial GVA. Check: the derived NW and Central GDP shares reproduce the published 11.5 % and 10.7 % (see report.json). District level: each provincial sector total is split over its districts in proportion to LFS 2024 Table 13 employment in that sector (agriculture) or that employment x HIES 2019 mean monthly household income of the district (industry, services; a relative productivity proxy, because LFS counts workers where they live). Net taxes follow district GVA. Districts sum exactly to provinces and the national total equals DCS GDP. Converted at the World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF 2024 average rate. Allocation to hexes: population-weighted within each district. gdp_usd = GVA at basic prices + net taxes on products = GDP at market prices. metrics.label: GDP per capita
metrics.description: GDP per resident at current prices.
metrics.method: gdp_usd of the county/district divided by its 2023 population used by the core grid (US Census PEP vintage 2023; Sri Lanka DCS mid-2023 estimates via COD-PS). Workplace-based GDP over resident population: commuter hubs (e.g. Colombo, Manhattan, DC) are inflated.

metrics.label: Median household income
metrics.description: Median annual household income, current US dollars of the survey year.
metrics.method: USA: ACS 2020-2024 5-year B19013_E001 (median household income in the past 12 months, 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars), county. | Sri Lanka: HIES 2019 Final Results Table 01, district MEDIAN monthly household income (Rs, all income incl. in-kind and imputed rent of owner-occupied housing) x 12, converted at the World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF 2019 average rate. Different survey years (2019 vs 2024 $) and income concepts: compare levels with care (no PPP adjustment applied).

metrics.label: Poverty rate
metrics.description: Share of people living below the national official poverty line.
metrics.method: USA: ACS 5-year B17001_E002 / B17001_E001 x 100 (people below the Census Bureau's income-based official poverty thresholds, by family size/composition; universe = people for whom poverty status is determined). | Sri Lanka: DCS Poverty Indicators 2019 Table 04 headcount index under the UPDATED official poverty line (consumption-based, Rs 6,966 per person per month in 2019, cost-of-basic-needs at 2,030 kcal). The two national lines are very different absolute standards (the US threshold is roughly 10x higher in dollars), so rates are comparable only within each country.

metrics.label: People in poverty
metrics.description: Number of people below the national official poverty line.
metrics.method: USA: ACS 5-year B17001_E002. | Sri Lanka: Poverty Indicators 2019 Table 04, number of poor people under the updated official poverty line. Same definitional caveats as poverty_rate.

metrics.label: Tropical cyclone passes (1980-2026)
metrics.description: Number of distinct tropical cyclones whose track passed within 100 km of the hex centre at tropical-storm strength or more, 1980 season to the latest (provisional) 2026 track.
metrics.method: IBTrACS since1980 list: main, PROVISIONAL and US-PROVISIONAL tracks (spurs dropped), points filtered to a box 5 deg around the country.  Wind = USA_WIND (1-min sustained, JTWC/NHC/CPHC) if reported, else WMO_WIND (agency-specific averaging, e.g. IMD 3-min, RSMC Tokyo 10-min).  A track point qualifies if NATURE is not ET (extratropical) or DS (disturbance) and wind >= 34 kt, or - when no wind is reported - NATURE = 'TS'.  Consecutive points of a storm (<= 6 h apart) are densified to <= 10 km steps (great-circle interpolation of position, linear interpolation of wind) so fast storms are not missed between 3-hourly fixes.  Count = distinct SIDs with any qualifying point within 100 km.  Exposure frequency at a point (not additive across hexes). Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Strongest cyclone wind nearby (1980-2026)
metrics.description: Highest maximum sustained wind (knots) of any qualifying tropical cyclone while its track was within 100 km of the hex centre.
metrics.method: Max of the (interpolated) track-point wind over the qualifying points counted in cyclone_tracks.  USA_WIND (1-min) preferred, WMO_WIND fallback.  0 = no qualifying pass. Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: M5+ earthquakes within 100 km (1976-2025)
metrics.description: Number of magnitude >= 5.0 earthquakes with epicentre within 100 km of the hex centre, 1 Jan 1976 - 31 Dec 2025 (any depth).
metrics.method: USGS ComCat FDSN CSV (preferred magnitude 'mag', any magType; eventtype=earthquake), deduplicated by event id across overlapping search boxes.  Exposure frequency at a point (not additive). Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Largest earthquake within 100 km (1976-2025)
metrics.description: Largest magnitude among the M5+ earthquakes within 100 km of the hex centre.
metrics.method: Max of ComCat preferred magnitude over events counted in quakes_m5.  0 = no M5+ event. Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Tsunami runup observations within 25 km (1900-2026)
metrics.description: Number of NOAA NCEI tsunami runup / tide-gauge observations located within 25 km of the hex centre since 1900.
metrics.method: HazEL runups API, boxes around each country (no country filter, so cross-border runups count). Kept: year >= 1900 and source event validity >= 3 (probable or definite tsunami; seiches, doubtful and erroneous events dropped).  Each runup record counts once (one tsunami usually produces several records along a coast). Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Tsunamis observed within 25 km (1900-2026)
metrics.description: Number of distinct tsunamis (source events) with at least one NOAA NCEI runup / tide-gauge observation within 25 km of the hex centre since 1900.
metrics.method: Same runup records as tsunami_runups, counted by distinct tsunamiEventId instead of by record, so a heavily surveyed single event (e.g. the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami along Sri Lanka's coast) counts once.  A frequency measure, used in hazard_index. Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Highest tsunami water height within 25 km (1900-2026)
metrics.description: Maximum tsunami water height (runup or tide-gauge amplitude, metres) among the observations counted in tsunami_runups.
metrics.method: Max of runupHt over the kept runup records; records without a height are counted but do not set the maximum.  0 = no observation with a height. Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Natural hazard index
metrics.description: Composite 0-100 exposure to tropical cyclones, strong earthquakes and tsunamis, on one scale for both countries (100 = most exposed).
metrics.method: Three event-frequency inputs: cyclone_tracks, quakes_m5 and tsunami_events (distinct tsunamis, not runup records).  For each input, a hex with 0 events scores 0; a hex with >= 1 event scores the mid-rank percentile of its value among all LAND hexes of BOTH countries (Sri Lanka res-6 + USA res-5 pooled) that have >= 1 event of that hazard: (n_below + 0.5 n_equal) / n_exposed.  Ranking among exposed hexes only keeps a single storm in 47 years from scoring like a hurricane coast just because most US hexes see none.  hazard_index = 100 x mean of the three scores, so a place exposed to only one hazard tops out near 33 and multi-hazard coasts (Hawaii, Alaska, California) score highest.  The reference distribution is pooled, so values are comparable between countries (inputs are radius counts, independent of hex size).  Floods, droughts, landslides, wildfire and tornadoes are not in this index (no consistent hex-level catalogue for both countries); see the admin tables for those.

metrics.label: FEMA National Risk Index score
metrics.description: FEMA National Risk Index composite risk score (0-100): a county's percentile-based score of NRI risk (expected annual loss from 18 natural hazards, scaled by social vulnerability and community resilience) relative to all US counties.
metrics.method: Field RISK_SCORE of the NRI Counties feature layer (NRI_VER 'December 2025'), joined on STCOFIPS = county GEOID (cb_2023 geography; no splitting needed).  The score ranks counties within the USA only, so it has no Sri Lankan counterpart.

metrics.label: Expected annual loss from natural hazards (FEMA NRI)
metrics.description: FEMA NRI expected annual loss, all 18 hazards: buildings + population (statistical value of life equivalence) + agriculture, in dollars per year.
metrics.method: Field EAL_VALT (Expected Annual Loss - Total - Composite; the 18 hazards are avalanche, coastal flooding, cold wave, drought, earthquake, hail, heat wave, hurricane, ice storm, landslide, lightning, inland flooding, strong wind, tornado, tsunami, volcanic activity, wildfire, winter weather), joined on STCOFIPS.  Dollar basis as published by FEMA for the December 2025 release (Hazus building inventory, value of a statistical life) - not re-based.  Allocated to hexes by population.

metrics.label: Expected annual loss: coastal flooding (FEMA NRI)
metrics.description: FEMA NRI expected annual loss from coastal flooding.
metrics.method: Field CFLD_EALT, joined on STCOFIPS; NULL where FEMA rates the hazard 'Not Applicable' (no coastline) -> 0.  Allocated to hexes with the coast weight.

metrics.label: Expected annual loss: inland (riverine) flooding (FEMA NRI)
metrics.description: FEMA NRI expected annual loss from inland flooding (published as 'Riverine Flooding' in earlier NRI releases).
metrics.method: Field IFLD_EALT ('Inland Flooding - Expected Annual Loss - Total'). metrics.label: Research works 2021-2025
metrics.description: Scholarly works (articles, reviews, books, conference papers, preprints, reports...) published 2021-2025 with an author affiliated to research institutions located in the hex.
metrics.method: OpenAlex institution points. research_works_5y = number of works published 2021-2025 of type article, review, book, book-chapter, conference-paper, preprint, report, dissertation, letter, data-paper, software-paper with an authorship affiliated to the institution (works?filter=authorships.institutions.id:<id>,publication_year:2021-2025,type:...; meta.count). Datasets, peer reviews, errata, editorials, conference abstracts, book reviews, paratext, software and 'other' are excluded: in 2021-2025 OpenAlex lists 1.8 M US datasets, most deposited by a few institutions (PNNL 1.17 M). Column works_5y keeps the all-types counts_by_year total for reference. A co-authored work counts once for every participating institution, so sums over hexes or the nation exceed the number of distinct works; preprints and their published versions can both count. Parent organisations do not roll up their children in OpenAlex (works are counted on the institution id, not its lineage), so there is no hierarchy double counting. Points sit at the Wikidata campus coordinate (item with the institution's ROR ID, nearest P625 within 50 km of the OpenAlex point) or, failing that, at the OpenAlex/GeoNames city point (column coord_source). Reconcile sums the points per hex. Sri Lanka: all 141 OpenAlex institutions with country_code LK. United States: institutions with more than 200 lifetime works (6,834 of 35,768), which excludes only the long tail of small organisations.

metrics.label: University R&D expenditure (HERD FY2024)
metrics.description: Total R&D expenditures of the higher-education institution (all sources of funds).
metrics.method: NSF HERD FY2024 Table 5 'All R&D expenditures' (dollars in thousands x 1000), 50 states + DC. System subtotal rows are dropped (a row is a subtotal when it equals the sum of its indented children; superscript footnote markers removed). Institutions are matched to OpenAlex education/healthcare/nonprofit/facility/government institutions by normalised name within the same state (U./C./Inst./Sch./Med./St. expanded, SUNY/CUNY prefixes dropped): exact token match, then names that differ only by a place qualifier (after a comma, dash or 'at', or a state name), then fuzzy >= 0.86; one-to-one, greedy by score then R&D. 21 manual assignments (science.HERD_ASSIGN); where HERD reports campuses jointly (U. Maryland = College Park + Baltimore per Table 5 footnote b; Texas A&M + Health Science Center; Penn State + Hershey; Vanderbilt + VUMC; Nebraska-Lincoln + UNMC; Dartmouth + Dartmouth-Hitchcock) the R&D is split in proportion to each campus's 2021-2025 research works (an estimate). 99.8% of HERD R&D and all top-100 institutions are matched; matches are listed in herd_matches.csv.

metrics.label: Mean elevation
metrics.description: Mean height of the land surface in the hex (DSM, metres above EGM2008 geoid).
metrics.method: Copernicus GLO-90 DSM pixels assigned to the H3 hex whose boundary contains the pixel centre (H3 polygons rasterised on each DEM tile grid). Sri Lanka: native 3 arc-sec (~90 m) tiles; USA: the COG's 4x internal overview (12 arc-sec N-S, ~370 m; coarser E-W spacing north of 50N follows the GLO tiling; average-downsampled, so peaks are smoothed), read with GDAL /vsicurl/. Statistics use land pixels only (DEM != 0; ocean is 0 m and absent tiles are sea); hexes without land pixels get 0 m and 0 deg. Means are weighted by pixel area. DSM heights include canopy/buildings, relative to the EGM2008 geoid. Border hexes are described as whole tiles (foreign land inside a US border hex is included).

metrics.label: Mean slope
metrics.description: Average terrain slope of land pixels in the hex.
metrics.method: Copernicus GLO-90 DSM pixels assigned to the H3 hex whose boundary contains the pixel centre (H3 polygons rasterised on each DEM tile grid). Sri Lanka: native 3 arc-sec (~90 m) tiles; USA: the COG's 4x internal overview (12 arc-sec N-S, ~370 m; coarser E-W spacing north of 50N follows the GLO tiling; average-downsampled, so peaks are smoothed), read with GDAL /vsicurl/. Statistics use land pixels only (DEM != 0; ocean is 0 m and absent tiles are sea); hexes without land pixels get 0 m and 0 deg. Means are weighted by pixel area. DSM heights include canopy/buildings, relative to the EGM2008 geoid. Border hexes are described as whole tiles (foreign land inside a US border hex is included). Slope = atan(|grad z|) from central differences (numpy.gradient) on the sampled DEM grid with metric pixel spacing (dx = deg x 111.32 km x cos(lat), dy = deg x 110.57 km), one-sided at tile edges, averaged over the hex's land pixels. Approximate: on the ~370 m US grid slopes are systematically lower than on 90 m (LKA) or 30 m DEMs, so compare slopes within a country.

metrics.label: Land cover: Tree cover
metrics.description: Fraction (0-1) of the hex covered by ESA WorldCover class 10 'Tree cover'.
metrics.method: Share of the hex's pixels in WorldCover class 10 (Tree cover). WorldCover pixels (Sri Lanka: all native 10 m pixels; USA: the COG's 8x internal overview, 0.00067 deg ~ 80 m, which GDAL built with mode resampling, so locally dominant classes are over-represented by ~1 percentage point and scattered minority classes such as built-up slightly under-represented) are assigned to the hex containing their centre (rasterised H3 polygons); fractions are over the whole hex area, so the 11 classes sum to 1. Open ocean (no-data 0 inside tiles, or no tile at all) is counted as water (class 80). Border hexes are described as whole tiles (foreign land included); the *_km2 weights are in-country only.

metrics.label: Mean annual temperature

metrics.method: BIO1 (annual mean temperature, deg C) of the WorldClim 2.1 1970-2000 normals, nearest-pixel value at the centres of the hex's H3 children (res+2, 49 points/hex), averaged over points with data, on the 2.5 arc-min grid (~4.6 km) for both countries.
